messages:
shreya: heads-up — ran into a weird HF->Redwood chat_template conversion bug while onboarding a new model. quick repro below, short thread.

matt: ok drop the repro, which model / tokenizer / quant?

shreya: model: `eleuther/ti-13b` + conversion to our 8-bit quant variant. tokenizer is HF Roberta-like with extra special tokens. config.json and chat_template are standard. repro: run `python tools/convert_chat_template.py --from hf --to redwood sample_chat_template.jinja`

shreya: here's the snippet from the HF chat_template (shortened):
```
{% chat_template %}
- role: system
  content: |-
    You are a helpful assistant.
- role: user
  content: |-
    Translate the text below to Spanish:
    ```translate
    "Hello, how are you?"  # nested literal block with quoted markers
    ```
- role: assistant
  content: |-
    (should be generated)
{% endchat_template %}
```

shreya: expected after conversion: explicit assistant marker preserved and template becomes Redwood prompt with sentinel markers. actual: assistant block collapsed into previous user content and the assistant sentinel was stripped. final prompt sent to runtime looked like:
```
System: You are a helpful assistant.
User: Translate the text below to Spanish:\n```translate\n"Hello, how are you?"\n```\n
```
(— no Assistant: section)
```

alexa: huh. sounds like the triple-backtick `translate` rawblock caused the converter to consider the following assistant role as contiguous text. did tokenizer tokenize backticks or special tokens differently?

shreya: looks like it. special_tokens_map.json has "additional_special_tokens": ["```translate", "```"] added by the HF template author. but in our convert pipeline we first run jinja render which collapses rawblocks, then we run role-splitting by searching for role markers. because the rawblock contains role-like delimiters inside a quoted literal, our naive splitter merges lines.

liam: can you paste the converter snippet that does splitting? maybe we can make it sensitive to fenced code rawblocks.

shreya: sure — key part:
```
# VERY simplified
rendered = jinja_env.render(template)
parts = re.split(r"^(- role: \w+)", rendered, flags=re.M)
# then we map role lines -> Redwood markers
```

liam: regex is brittle. if jinja preserves the fenced block markers as inline text, the `^(- role: \w+)` still matches but line offsets shift. also `additional_special_tokens` containing backticks is unexpected.

matt: two action items: (1) make the splitter ignore content inside fenced code blocks (pre-parse fences), (2) avoid treating triple-backtick variants as special tokens in tokenizer addition unless explicitly needed. agree?

alexa: +1 on both. quick patch idea: run a pass that replaces fenced blocks with placeholders before role-splitting, then restore. placeholder must be unique and escaped so our sentinel generator won't accidentally unescape it. something like `__FENCE_42__`.

shreya: tried a local hack — it fixes the assistant-preserve problem for this example. but there's a thornier variant: when the nested block contains characters that our tokenizer maps to multi-byte sentinel sequences (e.g., custom special tokens), the placeholder approach needs to run before tokenizer augmentation.

matt: OK. also we should add a unit test for chat_template fixtures that include nested fenced blocks and quoted markers. add an eval that checks final prompt contains an Assistant sentinel line.

eva: FYI this surfaced a regression in our quant eval: for the model onboarding run, the dialogue-coherence-v2 suite dropped ~8% in exact-match when the assistant marker was missing — model looked like it hallucinated context because messages concatenated. linking eval logs: https://internal.redwood/evals/ti-13b/2024-11-08

shreya: ops-bot created an internal ticket and a draft PR: RW-INC-8213, PR #4927 (wip). patch details in PR: placeholder fenced-block pass, adjusted order of ops: render -> fence-placeholder -> role-split -> restore -> tokenizer-augment.

ops-bot: Incident created: RW-INC-8213. Assigned to: shreya, liam. Priority: P2.

matt: can we also add a small fuzz test: generate random jinja templates with nested fenced blocks and run convert -> parse -> roundtrip check that roles preserved. if flaky, fail CI for converter.

shreya: gonna add fuzz + unit. note: also hit weirdness with `|safe` filters — they suppress escaping and can reintroduce markers in unexpected places. I'll add a test case for `{{ my_block|safe }}`.

alexa: nice catch. once PR is ready ping infra for a canary on dedicated so we can run the full quantized eval (8-bit) — we want to ensure the fix doesn't change tokenization/quant alignment.

liam: timeline?

shreya: small PR today, tests tomorrow, canary by EOD Thu. If all green, we'll roll to staging and re-run dialogue-coherence-v2 and unit-cost benchmarks.

matt: thanks; this explains the regression spike in the onboarding dashboard. please pin the failing eval logs in the PR. :thumbsup: 

eva: adding a regression alert (dialogue-coherence-v2) so we don't miss future appearances.

shreya: cool. I'll follow up with a short engineer note in the onboarding docs about not adding triple-backtick tokens to `additional_special_tokens`.
